headline: GOLD STEADIES AT $4,464 MONDAY — Warsh Shock Absorbed As September Rate Hike Odds Ease From 60% Peak
snippet: Gold stabilised at $4,464.65/oz (+0.2%) on Monday after plunging more than 3% on August 31 as institutional buyers absorbed the Warsh hawkishness — two-year Treasury yields stabilised after Friday's 12bp surge, and September rate hike odds eased from a peak of 64% toward 57%. Analysts note that August's 9.6% gold gain remains intact and central bank buying activity is evident, with the strength of the two-week rebound prior to Warsh's speech suggesting sovereign wealth funds were active at lower prices.

headline: GOLD STOCKS' AUTUMN RALLY WINDOW OPENS — September Seasonal Peak Historically Precedes A 15-25% Winter Run
snippet: GoldSeek's seasonal analysis argues that gold stocks are entering their most reliable rally window of the year: major gold stocks have historically averaged strong September gains before a brief October consolidation sets up the winter run. At GDX's current 16.5x trailing earnings — a multi-decade valuation low — the combination of seasonal tailwinds, record AISC margins, and the post-Warsh selloff entry point argues for adding junior exposure before the seasonal peak.

headline: CHINA HOARDING SILVER: 790+ TONNES IMPORTED IN EARLY 2026 — SWOT Data Shows Strategic Bid Far Above Historical Norms
snippet: The weekly Gold SWOT report flags China's 790+ metric-tonne silver import volumes in early 2026 as a structural demand signal well above historical norms, driven by solar panel production, EV battery components, and semiconductor fabrication. The data underpins silver's relative outperformance versus gold during the August 31 Warsh/Iran shock — silver's industrial demand floor absorbed selling pressure that pushed gold down 3%+, a divergence analysts say is a leading indicator of further silver strength as deficit projections (sixth consecutive annual shortfall) tighten available exchange stocks.

headline: SEPTEMBER GOLD OUTLOOK: WILL 9.6% AUGUST GAIN HOLD AGAINST 64% RATE HIKE ODDS AND $4,200 TEST RISK?
snippet: A September gold price forecast survey maps the bull and bear cases following Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole address: the bull case rests on central bank buying acting as a structural floor with sub-$4,300 gold historically triggering sovereign accumulation, while the bear case centres on a surprise September FOMC hike that forces speculative long liquidation from historically elevated COT positioning — potentially testing $4,200–$4,250 support before the next leg higher.

headline: COPPER HOLDS $14,800 AS GRASBERG + KAMOA-KAKULA REMOVE 600K TONNES FROM 2026 SUPPLY
snippet: Copper sustained above $14,800/tonne Monday near its all-time high as the supply crisis deepens: Grasberg's mudslide force majeure removes nearly 600,000 tonnes of refined copper from the 2026 schedule through year-end, Ivanhoe Mines cut Kamoa-Kakula's 2026 guidance from 380,000–420,000 to 290,000–330,000 tonnes in April, and Zijin Mining warned in late August that flooding could trim its share by an additional 57,000 tonnes — making 2025–26 the weakest two-year supply growth period since 2011 even as electrification and AI data centre demand continue to expand.

headline: BMI HIKES COPPER FORECAST 6.7% — Structural Deficit Seen Widening To 1.5M Tonnes By 2035, $17,000/T Target
snippet: BMI (Fitch's commodity research unit) raised its copper price forecasts 6.7% across its long-term model after supply disruptions tightened the 2026 balance further than prior projections assumed, projecting a deficit that widens from 66,000 tonnes in 2027 to nearly 1.5 million tonnes by 2035 as EV, offshore wind, and AI data centre demand outpaces committed new mine supply. The revised price path reaches $13,500/tonne in 2028, $15,000 in 2029, $15,800 in 2030, and $17,000 by 2035 — above Wall Street consensus and a direct read-through to the undeveloped copper resource valuations currently embedded in junior copper explorers.

headline: WISDOMTREE: GOLD MINERS CASE BUILDING 'BENEATH THE SURFACE' — Record FCF, Sub-16x Earnings, Equity Re-Rating Lagging Gold
snippet: WisdomTree's sector analysis documents the gap between gold's 70% year-on-year price rise and gold equities' more modest re-rating — pointing to sub-40% AISC-to-gold-price ratios held for multiple consecutive quarters and record free cash flow margins as evidence of fundamental undervaluation that the market has not yet fully discounted. The analysis argues the post-Warsh selloff represents an entry point before the equity catch-up to underlying metal and earnings power, with GDX's historically low P/E ratio providing a margin of safety if September FOMC hawkishness creates short-term volatility.

headline: LITHIUM LEADS, COBALT DIVERGES: CREDENDO MAPS BATTERY METALS SPLIT — DRC Export Quota Risk Widens Cobalt Deficit To 25%+
snippet: Credendo's battery metals market update maps 2026's growing divergence: lithium carbonate doubled after China's VAT export rebate cut forced supply adjustment, cobalt rose approximately 130% but the IEA now projects the supply gap widening from just over 15% to more than 25% as the Democratic Republic of Congo's export quotas constrain available feedstock, and nickel remains under structural pressure from high-cost Indonesian oversupply. The cobalt supply constraint — less publicly discussed than lithium's recovery — may represent the best risk-adjusted opportunity in battery metals if DRC quota tightening accelerates faster than consensus anticipates.

headline: MP MATERIALS, USA RARE EARTH, LYNAS: 3 WESTERN STOCKS TO WATCH AS WASHINGTON'S TRADE MOVES RESHAPE SUPPLY CHAIN
snippet: Following Washington's latest trade actions targeting Chinese rare earth supply chains, analysis identifies MP Materials (NYSE: MP), USA Rare Earth (NASDAQ: USAR), and Lynas Rare Earths (ASX: LYC) as the three Western equities best positioned to benefit — citing MP's DoD price floor agreement and $500M Apple supply deal, USA Rare Earth's Oklahoma magnet manufacturing facility targeting dysprosium and terbium, and Lynas's $96M Pentagon oxide supply contract and $110/kg NdPr price floor. All three trade at premium valuations that reflect strategic national-security demand rather than purely commercial rare earth pricing.

headline: SPROTT URANIUM: INVESTORS ACTING WITH CONVICTION — US Utilities Only 30% Contracted vs. Historical 70-80% Norm
snippet: Sprott's uranium watch documents institutional investors building uranium positions with conviction as US utilities remain approximately 30% contracted against their 10-year requirements — far below the historical 70–80% norm — driving term prices toward $100/lb while spot holds above $90/lb. The sustained term premium above spot reflects utilities paying a forward security premium rather than relying on thin spot availability, a market structure that has historically supported uranium equity valuations well above what spot price alone would imply, particularly for Western-jurisdiction producers like Cameco and Athabasca Basin developers.
